methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $235M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Electra.aero is a Series B-stage transportation company that has raised $235M to date. The broader Transportation sector includes eight private peers—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems—with no public comparables available. A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints meeting valuation-tier filters within the transportation cohort.

Stage-progression methodology anchors the valuation framework. Using total capital raised ($235M) as a proxy for implied post-money valuation and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage transitions yields $446M. This method is applicable given the company's defined stage and fundraising history.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $380M to $513M, with a median of $446M. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty. The absence of tight peer comparables in Transportation at comparable stages limits cross-validation. Key uncertainties include unit economics trajectory, capital efficiency relative to the peer set, and near-term milestone achievement. Any valuation within the derived range should be stress-tested against Electra.aero's specific operational metrics and burn profile relative to the broader private transportation cohort, though quantitative peer benchmarking remains constrained by data availability.
